summary: Pierce County, WA crow's nest in a tree near Purdy, possibly topped and given a platform in WWII; 1942 staffing reported second-hand; gone by 1952; private land today.

facts.design: Lookout tree (crow's nest), topped and fitted with a small platform; a 1940s list calls it a framed timber lookout
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com marks it gone; Kingsbury's recollection is that it was already gone by 1952. No removal date is given.

access.note: The 10 acres named in AWS documents is private property with home sites, per Willhite's 2017 visit

visit.trail_note: Nothing remains described to climb. The land is private and no public access is described.

facts.agency: Port Orchard District (warden D. Fraser), per a 1940s list

events.note: Charles R. Siegel, Jr. reportedly staffed it in summer 1942, per a friend's account given to Willhite in 2017 (second-hand)
John Kingsbury, working out of the Port Orchard office in 1952, believed the lookout was gone by then; recollection, not a record

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and its index call it a crow's nest; the 1940s list calls it a framed timber lookout. Willhite's notes read it as a lookout tree, perhaps later with a framed structure. The story reports both.
Firelookout.com dates the crow's nest to the 1930s; Fraser's recollection places the topping and platform in the early part of the war. Not reconciled; the story gives both.
Willhite's page spells the interviewee Don Lee Frazier in one place and Donald Lee Fraser elsewhere; the story uses Fraser.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' is supported. Access changed from unknown to private on the 2017 visit. The 1942 staffing is a second-hand account relayed to Willhite, so the story says reported. Kingsbury's 1952 view is a recollection (he was interviewed in 2017); the Fraser account is from a 2019 VHS interview. No height is given because the only figure is Kingsbury's estimate of the tree. Brief kind 'platform' fits the crow's nest description; left unchanged.
